newsitem.title: UK: Dlr soars, Eurobourses mixed as Dow drops.
newsitem.headline: Dlr soars, Eurobourses mixed as Dow drops.

text.p: The dollar surged on Monday, climbing to a four-year high against the Swiss franc, an eight-year peak against the French franc and mark and nearly a 12-year high against the lira on nervousness over German interest rates.

Interest rate jitters, coupled with corporate earnings, also kept European stocks mixed in the afternoon and forced the Dow Jones Industrial Average to open lower. But Finnish shares managed to eke out a record high after impressive earnings results from Nokia Ab, Oy's.
The dollar jumped on speculation the Federal Reserve will have to raise interest rates at its next policy-making meeting on August 19 and uncertainty surrounding the German central bank's next move.

After a 316,000 rise in U.S. July nonfarm payrolls and a rise above 50 for the first time in four months in the National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) July prices paid index on Friday, traders were starting to price in an imminent rise in official U.S. interest rates.
A rise above 50 in the NAPM index usually points to expansion, while a figure below 50 indicates contraction.
That, coupled with doubts over German monetary policy, propelled the dollar higher, traders said.

Before leaving for its four-week summer recess, the Bundesbank set its weekly money market operations at a fixed 3.0 percent for two weeks. Traders speculated the Bundesbank was leaving room for rates to drift higher in the last two holiday weeks by setting a variable rate tender.

Talk even circulated that the German central bank would not wait two weeks before setting a variable rate tender. Instead, it could set a second money market operation this week in addition to its fixed-rate tender depending on key German jobless data due on Wednesday.
But most traders dismissed such talk, saying that Germany's fragile economy could break under the weight of higher rates.
Though the dollar benefitted from interest rate speculation, stocks did not fare as well.
Uncertainty about Bundesbank policy rattled Germany's blue-chip DAX index. The DAX ended bourse trade down 111.85 points, or more than 2.50 percent, at 4,296.94.

Bank shares led the declines. Commerzbank AG was down 1.15 marks at 61.50, Deutsche Bank AG down 4.75 at 117.40, Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG down 3.90 at 72.05 and Bay Vereinsbank was down 3.00 at 95.80.
London's FTSE-100 index extended losses after the Dow opened weak and quickly extended losses to set off the New York Stock Exchange's trading curbs.
After the first hour of trading, the Dow was down 51.80 points at 8,142.24, adding to Friday's losses on strong U.S. data.
But FTSE losses were limited by HSBC Holdings Plc 's jump to a year high of 2,326 pence on better-than-expected first-half results.

The bank said pre-tax profits in sterling terms rose 13 percent to 2.623 billion pounds ($4.3 billion), with dividends up 33 percent to 20 pence per share. That compares with analysts' forecasts for pre-tax profits between 2.32 and 2.48 billion pounds.
FTSE activity was also expected to be limited with interest rate worries looming. The Bank of England's monetary policy-setting meeting is on Wednesday and Thursday.
A Reuters poll taken on July 30 showed 16 of 23 economists expected official British interest rates to rise 25 basis points after the meeting for the fourth rate rise in so many months.
French shares also extended losses below 3,000 as Wall Street tumbled.
Finland's FOX index was an exception, scoring a record high after Nokia's first-half earnings report.
The mobile phone maker said first-half profits of 3.33 billion markka ($5.9 billion) to beat a Reuters survey of expectations for 3.09 billion and the highest forecast in the survey of 3.3 billion.
Nokia shares hit a year high of 485 markka in early trade, and the FOX index was up 3.40 at 1,241.58, just off its record 1,244.41.
Dutch stocks erased early gains to end lower as New York shares fell and traders searched for the next market trend.
"There's some fear in the market. People are no longer that convinced (of the uptrend). They're looking for a direction," a dealer said.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8640 marks and 118.22 yen compared to 1.8630 and 118.37 in late trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 12.1 points at 4,887.20.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended bourse trade down 111.85 points at 4,296.94. The DAX IBIS index was down 34.48 points at 4,302.50 in electronic trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 57.03 points at 2,992.41.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at 1500 in London at $323.55, down from Friday's close at $324.25. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds) ($ = 5.552 Finnish Markka)
